findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is a rubber stamp: `z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()` both evaluate to `"[object Object]"`, so the keys collide and the schema is really `{access_token: string, "[object Object]"?: unknown}`. The "any numeric property is the expiry" rule doesn't exist, and zod strips everything else — so on the sync path `.data` is *only* `{access_token}`. A totally broken sync endpoint reports "valid tokens" while the caller persists a gutted credential.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:26 — Poison pill: when `refresh_token` is absent (always, on the sync path, per #1) the literal string `"refresh_token"` is written into the returned data. `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264` spreads it into `credential.key`, permanently overwriting the user's real Microsoft refresh token. Next refresh POSTs `refresh_token=refresh_token` → `invalid_grant`, unrecoverable without full re-OAuth. No rollback — the real token is gone.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the zod SafeParse **envelope** (`{success, data}`), not the parsed key, but it's assigned to `key` and written to `credential.key` at line 100 (the replaced `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` returned the key itself). After one refresh the row becomes `{"success":true,"data":{…}}`, so `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` at line 75 throws forever. **Fires on the default path, sync disabled.**

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — `prisma.credential.update(...)` is called but `prisma` is never imported — imports end at line 20 with no `@calcom/prisma`. Every `SalesforceCalendarService` construction throws `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined`; the package also fails typecheck. Salesforce is dead on arrival.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:32 — The team branch authorizes with `members: { some: { userId, accepted: true } }` — membership only, **no role check**. Any accepted plain MEMBER can complete an OAuth flow with `state.teamId` set and install/overwrite the team-wide credential every other member's bookings then use (Stripe payouts, CRM, calendar). Privilege escalation.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:59 — `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam({teamId: state?.teamId ?? null, …})` is only reachable *after* the `if (state?.teamId) {…return}` early-return at line 30, so it is always called with `teamId: null`. The admin gate is dead code on the only path where a team exists — it reads as authorization while performing none.

Because the parameter is `() => any`, the return type collapses to `any` and TypeScript checks **none** of the six call sites. Root cause of #8–#12.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
